Ashok: quick q — for async iterable prefetching across Python/TS/Go: do we want 'transactional' semantics where fetch is tied to iterator checkpoint or a loose prefetch that may be in-flight on cancel? Pros/cons (idempotency + retries)
Marta: leaning toward transactional. simpler guarantees for consumer. But costs: cancels waste prefetched tokens and harder to do batching.
Sam: agree on simpler guarantees. For TS/Go we can expose cancel token that triggers negative ack and let server discard cached prefetch. For Python we have async iterator close semantics already.
Devon: edge case: retries on transient transport errors mid-page. If we tie prefetch to checkpoint, retry requires deterministic resume token or idempotent fetch. Otherwise we double-run.
June: propose: require resume token per page + prefetch window small (1 page). Also include an 'at-most-once' vs 'at-least-once' flag in SDK config.
Ashok: sketch of API (TS example):
```ts
const it = client.listEvents({ resumeToken: null, prefetchPages: 1, idempotency: 'resume-token' })
for await (const page of it) {
  // page.items
}
```
Marta: +1. Important: transports must propagate idempotency-key header for unary fetches, otherwise resume-token won't be enough if server dedups differently.
sdk-ci-bot: deploy notice — transport-proxy v2 canary will add header support: x-redwood-idempotency-key.
Sam: runtime concern: batching/continuous backend might consolidate requests. If we enforce transactional prefetch, batching could be reduced => cost up. Need heuristics: prefetch only when latency SLO allows.
Devon: TL;DR: propose default: resume-token + prefetch=1, idempotency header enabled. Advanced users can opt into prefetch>1 and 'best-effort' semantics. We should also add a 'resume-token' strong contract on the server.
Ashok: love it. can someone write a short RFC patch? assign to @Marta and @Sam. I'll follow up with perf quickchecks.
Marta: I'll put an initial doc in RFCs/ with sample server contract and transport header examples.
